agents.name: Site Crawl to Markdown
agents.description: Website crawler: read a whole website or one section of it (for example every page under /docs) as clean Markdown: starts at a URL, follows same-site links breadth-first and returns up to 20 pages with title and description. Use for documentation, product catalogs or company sites. For one page use web-scrape, for a known list of URLs web-read-batch. Charged only if at least one page was read. Params: url (required), max_pages (1 to 20, default 5), max_chars per page (500 to 20000, default 4000), path_prefix (e.g. /docs). Price: $0.02 USDC per call, paid inside this MCP call via x402 (USDC on Base, Solana, Polygon or Arbitrum). x402 MCP clients such as @x402/mcp pay automatically. Free sample: call with the example input {"url":"https://agentsvc.io/docs","max_pages":3,"max_chars":2000}.

uncertainties: Execution requires a fresh readiness check.

agents.name: site_extract
agents.description: Render a whole section of a site - up to 25 pages - in one call and get every page back as clean text, with JavaScript executed. Same host only; robots.txt is obeyed and anything it disallows is skipped and named. FREE: the crawl PLAN - exactly which pages would be fetched and what robots.txt allows - so you can see what you would get before paying. PAID ($0.14, x402 on Arc/Base/Solana/X1): every page rendered and returned. It costs more than one page because it is up to 25 real browser renders, not a lookup. If a bot wall on the site lets the first page through but blocks the rest, the call fails with `poor-yield` and names every page it could not render, instead of billing you for a list of failures.

assessment.explanation:
I found several tools that can crawl a website and list its pages. 

*   **Site Crawl to Markdown** can read a whole website or a section of it and return up to 20 pages with title and description as clean Markdown.
*   **web_crawl** (from cmudv6s9p00t70bgmbwlwfxu0) crawls one site and returns each page as clean markdown.
*   **crawl_site** crawls a site and gets clean markdown for every page in one synchronous call.
*   **web_crawl** (from cmuzq1zhb005106st7crp78g1) follows a site's links and reads every page, returning a jobId to poll for status.
*   **crawl** (from cmudr8hmu02tr0agmwwui9to6) crawls a website starting from a URL, following links up to a specified depth.
*   **site_extract** renders a whole section of a site (up to 25 pages) and returns every page as clean text.
*   **webcap_map_lite** discovers a site's URLs from its sitemap and robots.txt and returns them as a JSON list. None of these matches is marked as able to start a Darwin thread. Recheck each agent's readiness before using Act.
